PyJWT consumer imports RSA public keys.
No source PKCS7 EnvelopedData decrypt call identified.

packages.action: Document non-reachability; review compatibility before any separate major-version dependency change.

packages.name: PyJWT
actual_callpaths: portal/auth.py:151 get_unverified_header before signature verification; catches PyJWTError only.
portal/auth.py:168 decode with ALGORITHMS=['RS256'], configured issuer/audience, fresh options literal.
dashboard/dashboard_access.py:verify_token caps token at 16384 bytes, parses header and payload with duplicate-key rejection, uses RS256 only, fresh options literal, catches Exception.
portal/main.py:5907 unsigned decode is of the same already middleware-verified token, catches Exception, and can only lower privilege.

per_condition_triage.evidence: Portal header parse has the affected call and narrow exception catch. Token comes from request header or CF_Authorization cookie, not JSON body; actual proxy/server field limits and Python recursion threshold may prevent the published oversized nested-header trigger. Dashboard broadly catches failure.
per_condition_triage.impact_limit: Advisory's confirmed impact is request-level HTTP 500/logging, not worker death or authentication bypass.

per_condition_triage.evidence: Both consumers use custom requests JWKS loaders and RSAAlgorithm.from_jwk. Custom caching is not proof that PyJWKClient advisories apply; assess custom caching separately.
Portal verifying decode keeps signature verification enabled; its unsigned decode is post-verification and broadly caught. Dashboard separately parses untrusted payload but catches Exception.
RS256-only verification with imported RSA keys, not HS/asymmetric mixed allow-lists or empty oct JWK keys.
No shared options object reused between unsigned and signed decode in inspected call sites. Do not invent a fixed version.
Portal catches Exception for each RSAAlgorithm.from_jwk entry. Dashboard broadly catches loading errors and fails closed; only configured trusted JWKS can supply such keys.
RSA-only verifier; no attacker proof-header private OKP JWK import identified.
JWKS RSA key objects are supplied, rather than arbitrary client PEM text passed into the HMAC guard.
portal/main.py raw-token SHA256 is a catalogue cache key, not itself a revocation denial list. Do not infer a logout bypass from that cache.

packages.action: Scoped upgrade to at least 2.15.0 before runtime plus retain fresh-options mitigation; separately confirm portal transport bounds and clean handling of recursive headers.

packages.name: urllib3
actual_callpaths: portal/upstream.py:176 post_bytes uses requests.iter_content(65536), permits normal response decoding and caps output after each yield.
portal/upstream.py:267 stream_chunks uses iter_content; stream() requests identity and rejects non-identity encoding before yielding, mitigating the deflate-specific path for that GET route.
dashboard/dashboard_access.py:60 uses requests.iter_content(8192) for configured Cloudflare JWKS.
dashboard/main.py:8563 uses iter_content(16384) for fixed internal service-exceptions source.
conditions: Deflate loop requires chunked compressed response, positive finite chunk size, extra bytes after completed deflate stream and decoded body exceeding chunk size.
Chunk-size-line exhaustion requires malicious chunked upstream, independent of content-decoding negotiation.
Application byte limits/deadlines run after iteration yields and therefore do not eliminate parser-internal loop/buffering.

HTTPS proxy issue needs effective HTTPS proxy mode and specified proxy/target TLS configuration combinations. No custom ProxyManager or proxy SSL context call identified; requests environment proxy configuration remains unverified.
packages.action: High-priority scoped lock refresh before runtime. Treat endpoint compromise/on-path conditions explicitly; no arbitrary request-selected URL was established.

packages.name: python-multipart
evidence: dashboard/main.py:12749 /api/scan/upload uses FastAPI Form and File parameters.
Multipart extended name/filename interpretation is exposed through framework form parsing; actual smuggling impact needs an intermediary policy relying on a different parse.
Filename is passed through _safe_filename and path containment checks.
Endpoint requires files, so application/x-www-form-urlencoded parsing applicability and actual parser chunk size need framework verification before claiming the quadratic request impact.
No direct parse_form call found; negative Content-Length advisory explicitly excludes ordinary Starlette/FastAPI ASGI parsing.
packages.action: Scoped runtime dependency update before runtime; 0.0.31 is evidence-backed coverage, with 0.0.32 already used in sibling portal locks.
